We built Debate Sense, a web app where people in a room debate while AI transcribes and extracts claims for anonymous voting. Everything is working and pushed to GitHub. Next step is adding your OpenAI API key to the .env file to enable live transcription.

Now I have a thorough understanding of the entire codebase. Let me design the implementation plan. --- ## Detailed Implementation Plan: Voting UI Redesign for Debate Sense ### Architecture Overview The current codebase is small and clean: a FastAPI backend (`main.py`, `session.py`, `analysis.py`, `transcription.py`) and a React frontend (no router, no state library -- just `useState`/`useEffect` in `DebateRoom.jsx` which passes props down to `StatementsPanel.jsx`). Styles are in a single `index.css`. The project uses no charting library and no animation library, and the requirements explicitly say to keep it that way. The plan touches **4 frontend files** (1 replaced, 3 new), **1 backend file** (modified), and **1 CSS file** (extended). --- ### Part 1: Component Structure **Current flow:** `DebateRoom.jsx` holds `statements` state and `handleVote()`, passes both to `StatementsPanel.jsx` which renders all statements in a scrollable list. **New component tree:** ``` DebateRoom.jsx (modified: adds 3rd "Results" tab) | +-- StatementsPanel.jsx (REPLACED entirely) | | | +-- FlashCard.jsx (NEW: single unvoted statement card) | +-- DivergingBarChart.jsx (NEW: voted-statements bar chart) | +-- ResultsPanel.jsx (NEW: Polis-style placeholder) ``` **Component responsibilities:** 1. **`StatementsPanel.jsx`** -- Becomes a container/orchestrator. It receives `statements` and `onVote` as before (no API change from `DebateRoom`). It computes two derived lists: - `unvoted`: `statements.filter(s => !s.hasVoted)` -- feeds the first unvoted item to `FlashCard` - `voted`: `statements.filter(s => s.hasVoted)` -- feeds all to `DivergingBarChart` It also tracks a local `justVoted` state (the statement ID that was just voted on) so the bar chart knows which bar to entrance-animate. 2. **`FlashCard.jsx`** -- Receives a single statement object (or null). Renders the card with agree/disagree buttons. On vote, calls `onVote(id, vote)` and triggers exit animation via local state, then calls a callback (`onAnimationDone`) so `StatementsPanel` can advance to the next card. When no statement is provided, shows "All caught up -- waiting for more statements." 3. **`DivergingBarChart.jsx`** -- Receives the array of voted statements and `justVotedId`. Renders a diverging horizontal bar for each. Handles entrance animation for new bars and width-transition animation for vote count updates. 4. **`ResultsPanel.jsx`** -- A static placeholder component. Shows a mock scatter-plot SVG or illustration with "Polis-style clustering results will appear here after the debate." Conditionally shown via a new third tab in `DebateRoom`. --- ### Part 2: Changes to `DebateRoom.jsx` Minimal changes to keep the parent component stable: 1. **Add a third tab "Results"** to the tab bar. The `view` state already supports arbitrary string values. Add `'results'` as a third option. 2. **Update the conditional rendering block** (currently lines 204-229) to add a third branch: ``` view === 'results' ? : null ``` 3. **No other changes needed.** The `handleVote` function, WebSocket message handling, and `statements` state management all remain exactly as they are. The `vote_updated` handler (line 121-128) already updates individual statement objects in place -- this is what will drive real-time bar width animations in the chart. --- ### Part 3: New `StatementsPanel.jsx` (Full Replacement) The current 40-line component gets replaced entirely. The new version: ``` Props: { statements, onVote } State: - justVotedId: string | null (ID of the statement just voted on, cleared after animation) - exitingCard: boolean (true while the flash card is animating out) Derived: - unvoted = statements.filter(s => !s.hasVoted) - voted = statements.filter(s => s.hasVoted) - currentCard = exitingCard ? null : unvoted[0] || null handleCardVote(statementId, vote): 1. Set exitingCard = true (triggers CSS exit animation on FlashCard) 2. Call onVote(statementId, vote) -- sends WebSocket message 3. Set justVotedId = statementId 4. After animation delay (~300ms via setTimeout), set exitingCard = false (This causes React to render the next unvoted card, which entrance-animates via CSS) Render:
{voted.length > 0 && ( <>
Your votes
setJustVotedId(null)} /> )}
``` **Key design decision:** The `exitingCard` flag plus a setTimeout is simpler and more reliable than listening for `animationend` events in React. The 300ms delay matches the CSS animation duration. This avoids needing `useRef` callbacks or `onAnimationEnd` prop drilling. --- ### Part 4: `FlashCard.jsx` ``` Props: { statement, onVote, exiting } Render logic: - If statement is null and not exiting: return "All caught up" empty state (styled like existing .statements.empty) - Otherwise, render the card:

{statement.text}

``` **Animation approach:** Two CSS classes: - `.flash-card.enter`: `animation: slideInFromRight 0.3s ease-out` -- slides and fades in from the right - `.flash-card.exit`: `animation: slideOutToLeft 0.3s ease-in` -- slides and fades out to the left This gives the Tinder-like swipe feel without a gesture library. The buttons reuse the existing `.vote-btn` class with `.agree` / `.disagree` modifiers (lines 294-331 of `index.css`), so they inherit the existing hover/active styles. --- ### Part 5: `DivergingBarChart.jsx` This is the most complex new component. Here is the detailed design. ``` Props: { statements, justVotedId, onAnimationDone } For each statement: total = agrees + disagrees agreePercent = total > 0 ? (agrees / total) * 100 : 50 disagreePercent = total > 0 ? (disagrees / total) * 100 : 50 Render:
{statements.map(stmt => { const isNew = stmt.id === justVotedId return (
{ if (isNew) onAnimationDone() }} >

{truncate(stmt.text, 60)}

{stmt.disagrees}
{stmt.agrees}
{isNew && (
)}
) })}
``` **CSS layout for the diverging bar:** The `.bar-track` is a flex container with `display: flex; height: 28px; border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; background: #eee`. Inside it: - `.bar-disagree` grows from the LEFT: `background: #e00; display: flex; justify-content: flex-start; align-items: center; transition: width 0.6s ease-out` - `.bar-center-line`: a 2px wide absolute-positioned pseudo-element at 50% -- always visible - `.bar-agree` grows from the RIGHT: `background: #2a9d4e; display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; align-items: center; transition: width 0.6s ease-out` **Critical layout detail:** The bar-track uses a structure where disagree occupies from left-to-center and agree occupies from center-to-right. The implementation uses a different approach than a simple flex row -- instead, both bars are absolutely positioned within the track: ```css .bar-track { position: relative; height: 28px; background: #f0f0f0; border-radius: 4px; } .bar-disagree { position: absolute; right: 50%; height: 100%; background: rgba(238, 0, 0, 0.7); border-radius: 4px 0 0 4px; transition: width 0.6s ease-out; } .bar-agree { position: absolute; left: 50%; height: 100%; background: rgba(42, 157, 78, 0.7); border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0; transition: width 0.6s ease-out; } .bar-center-line { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 0; bottom: 0; width: 2px; background: #999; transform: translateX(-1px); z-index: 1; } ``` For the width calculation, each side's width is a percentage of **half** the track width. So if there are 3 agrees and 2 disagrees (total 5), agree-side width = `(3/5) * 50% = 30%` of the full track, disagree-side width = `(2/5) * 50% = 20%` of the full track. Actually, a cleaner model: each side's width is proportional to its count relative to the maximum of the two counts, scaled to fill at most 50% of the track. This way the larger side always fills its half, and the smaller side is proportionally shorter. Revised calculation: ```javascript const max = Math.max(stmt.agrees, stmt.disagrees, 1) const agreeWidth = (stmt.agrees / max) * 50 // percentage of track width const disagreeWidth = (stmt.disagrees / max) * 50 ``` This ensures the longer bar always extends to 50% (the center boundary) while the shorter one is proportionally scaled. The CSS `transition: width 0.6s` handles animated updates when `vote_updated` WebSocket messages arrive and React re-renders with new counts. **Bar count labels:** The `.bar-count` numbers sit at the outer ends of each bar: - Disagree count: positioned at the far left of the disagree bar - Agree count: positioned at the far right of the agree bar - If the bar is too narrow to contain the number, position it outside the bar **Entrance animation for new bars:** ```css @keyframes barEnter { from { opacity: 0; max-height: 0; transform: translateY(-10px); } to { opacity: 1; max-height: 80px; transform: translateY(0); } } .bar-row.bar-enter { animation: barEnter 0.4s ease-out; } ``` **Highlight pulse for "your vote counted":** ```css @keyframes votePulse { 0% { opacity: 0.6; } 50% { opacity: 0; } 100% { opacity: 0; } } .bar-highlight.agree { position: absolute; left: 50%; right: 0; background: #2a9d4e; animation: votePulse 0.8s ease-out; } .bar-highlight.disagree { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 50%; background: #e00; animation: votePulse 0.8s ease-out; } ``` This briefly flashes the user's vote side before fading out. **Real-time updates from other participants:** When a `vote_updated` WebSocket message arrives, `DebateRoom` updates the `statements` array (already works at line 121-128). The updated `agrees`/`disagrees` counts flow down as props, React re-renders `DivergingBarChart`, and the CSS `transition: width 0.6s` on `.bar-agree` / `.bar-disagree` makes the bars smoothly grow/shrink. --- ### Part 6: `ResultsPanel.jsx` (Polis Placeholder) A simple static component: ``` Props: { statements } Render:

Opinion Clusters

Polis-style opinion clustering will appear here after the debate concludes.

{statements.length} statements analyzed -- {statements.filter(s => s.hasVoted).length} voted

``` The SVG can be a simple inline illustration: a few colored circles in 2-3 clusters with dashed ellipses around them, giving a visual preview of what the Polis view will eventually show. --- ### Part 7: Backend -- Mock Auto-Play Endpoint **File:** `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/backend/app/main.py` Add a new endpoint `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/mock/auto` that drip-feeds entries from `MOCK_DEBATE` with ~2s delays as a background `asyncio` task. **Implementation:** 1. Add a dictionary to track running auto-play tasks: ```python auto_play_tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {} ``` 2. Add the drip-feed coroutine: ```python async def auto_play(session_id: str): idx = mock_index.get(session_id, 0) while idx < len(MOCK_DEBATE): session = sessions.get(session_id) if not session: break speaker, text = MOCK_DEBATE[idx] entry = { "type": "transcript", "text": text, "speaker": speaker, "timestamp": time.time(), } should_analyze = sessions.add_transcript_entry(session_id, entry) await sessions.broadcast(session_id, entry) idx += 1 mock_index[session_id] = idx if should_analyze: sessions.mark_analysis_started(session_id) asyncio.create_task(run_analysis(session_id)) await asyncio.sleep(2) # Clean up auto_play_tasks.pop(session_id, None) ``` 3. Add the endpoint: ```python @app.post("/api/sessions/{session_id}/mock/auto") async def mock_auto_play(session_id: str): session_id = session_id.upper() session = sessions.get(session_id) if not session: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Session not found") if session_id in auto_play_tasks and not auto_play_tasks[session_id].done(): return {"status": "already_running"} task = asyncio.create_task(auto_play(session_id)) auto_play_tasks[session_id] = task return {"status": "started", "entries": len(MOCK_DEBATE) - mock_index.get(session_id, 0)} ``` **Design note:** The auto-play coroutine checks `sessions.get(session_id)` each iteration so it stops if the session is deleted (all participants left). The 2-second delay between entries means the full 15-entry `MOCK_DEBATE` takes ~30 seconds. Analysis triggers every 3 entries (the existing `ANALYSIS_BATCH_SIZE = 3`), so there will be ~5 analysis runs spaced ~6 seconds apart -- plenty of time for the user to see statements trickle in and practice the voting flow. --- ### Part 8: CSS Approach All new styles go into `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/frontend/src/index.css`, appended after the existing styles. This maintains the single-stylesheet approach. **New CSS sections:** **A. Flash Card:** ```css /* Flash Card */ .flash-card { ... } /* card container, centered, max-width */ .flash-card.enter { animation: slideIn 0.3s ease-out; } .flash-card.exit { animation: slideOut 0.3s ease-in forwards; } .flash-card-text { ... } /* larger font, centered */ .flash-card-actions { ... } /* flex row, gap between buttons */ .flash-card-empty { ... } /* muted "all caught up" state */ @keyframes slideIn { ... } @keyframes slideOut { ... } ``` **B. Section divider:** ```css .section-divider { ... } /* "Your votes" text with horizontal lines */ ``` **C. Diverging Bar Chart:** ```css .bar-chart { ... } .bar-row { ... } .bar-row.bar-enter { animation: barEnter 0.4s ease-out; } .bar-label { ... } /* truncated text above bar */ .bar-track { ... } /* relative container */ .bar-disagree { ... } /* absolute, right: 50% */ .bar-agree { ... } /* absolute, left: 50% */ .bar-center-line { ... } .bar-count { ... } .bar-highlight { ... } @keyframes barEnter { ... } @keyframes votePulse { ... } ``` **D. Results placeholder:** ```css .results-panel { ... } .results-placeholder { ... } ``` **Mobile-first consideration:** The existing `#root { max-width: 600px }` already constrains the layout. The bar chart works well on narrow screens because: - The bar labels are truncated with ellipsis (`overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`) - The bar track always spans full width of the container - Count numbers use a small font size (0.75rem) and are positioned within or adjacent to bars - No horizontal scrolling needed --- ### Part 9: Animation Strategy Summary | Animation | Trigger | Technique | Duration | |---|---|---|---| | Card slide out | User taps Agree/Disagree | CSS `@keyframes slideOut` on `.flash-card.exit` | 300ms | | Card slide in | Next card appears | CSS `@keyframes slideIn` on `.flash-card.enter` | 300ms | | New bar entrance | Statement just voted on appears in chart | CSS `@keyframes barEnter` (opacity + max-height + translateY) | 400ms | | Bar grow from center | Initial bar render + count updates | CSS `transition: width 0.6s ease-out` on `.bar-agree`/`.bar-disagree` | 600ms | | Vote highlight pulse | User's own vote side | CSS `@keyframes votePulse` (opacity flash) | 800ms | | Other user vote update | `vote_updated` WebSocket msg | CSS `transition: width 0.6s` (bars auto-resize via style prop change) | 600ms | All animations use CSS only. No `requestAnimationFrame`, no JS animation libraries. The React component just toggles class names and inline `style.width` -- CSS handles the rest. --- ### Part 10: Implementation Order This sequence minimizes broken states and allows incremental testing: **Step 1: Backend -- Mock auto-play endpoint** (`main.py`) - Add `auto_play_tasks` dict, `auto_play()` coroutine, and `POST /mock/auto` endpoint - Test with `curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/sessions/XXXX/mock/auto` - Verify entries arrive 2s apart in the existing UI - This is independent of all frontend changes **Step 2: FlashCard component** (`FlashCard.jsx` + CSS) - Create the component with agree/disagree buttons - Add slideIn/slideOut keyframe animations to `index.css` - Temporarily render it standalone to test animations **Step 3: Replace StatementsPanel** (`StatementsPanel.jsx`) - Rewrite to split statements into unvoted/voted - Render `FlashCard` for the first unvoted statement - Wire up the exit/enter animation sequencing with `justVotedId` and `exitingCard` state - Test the full flashcard voting flow end-to-end **Step 4: DivergingBarChart component** (`DivergingBarChart.jsx` + CSS) - Build the bar layout with absolute positioning - Add the entrance animation for new bars - Add the highlight pulse for user's own vote - Verify that `transition: width` handles real-time updates from other participants **Step 5: Integrate chart into StatementsPanel** - Add `DivergingBarChart` below the `FlashCard` - Wire up `justVotedId` flow so bars animate in after voting - Test the complete flow: vote on flashcard -> card exits -> bar appears in chart with animation **Step 6: Results tab** (`ResultsPanel.jsx` + `DebateRoom.jsx` modification) - Create the placeholder component - Add the third "Results" tab in `DebateRoom.jsx` - Style it **Step 7: Polish and edge cases** - Test with 0 statements (empty state) - Test when all statements are voted on (caught-up message) - Test auto-play while voting (statements arriving mid-vote) - Verify mobile layout at various widths (320px to 600px) - Ensure the badge count in the tab still works (it reads `unvotedCount`) --- ### Edge Cases and Potential Challenges 1. **Race condition: voting while new statements arrive.** A `statements_updated` WebSocket message replaces the entire `statements` array. If the user votes on card N, and before the exit animation completes a `statements_updated` arrives, the `unvoted` list could shift. Mitigation: the `exitingCard` flag in `StatementsPanel` prevents advancing to the next card until the animation completes. The vote is already sent via WebSocket immediately, so even if the statements array updates, the server already has the vote. The `vote_updated` message will then mark it as `hasVoted: true`. 2. **Vote acknowledged after flashcard advances.** The user taps "Agree," the card animates out, and the next card appears. But the `vote_updated` message hasn't arrived yet, so the statement is still in `unvoted`. Mitigation: use optimistic local state. In `handleCardVote`, immediately mark the statement as voted locally (set a local `optimisticallyVoted` set of IDs) so the `unvoted` filter excludes it even before the server confirms. When `vote_updated` arrives and sets `hasVoted: true`, the optimistic state is no longer needed. 3. **Bar width when counts are both zero.** Impossible in practice (a bar only appears after the user votes, so at least one count is >= 1), but the `Math.max(..., 1)` in the width calculation handles it defensively. 4. **Long statement text in bar labels.** Truncated to ~60 chars with ellipsis via CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis`. The full text is visible in the flashcard before voting. 5. **Performance with many statements.** The bar chart re-renders all voted bars on every `vote_updated` message. With < 50 statements (realistic for a debate session), this is trivially fast. No virtualization needed. --- ### Critical Files for Implementation - `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/frontend/src/components/StatementsPanel.jsx` -- Full replacement: becomes the orchestrator that splits statements into flashcard + bar chart - `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/frontend/src/index.css` -- All new CSS: flashcard animations, diverging bar layout, bar animations, results placeholder styles - `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/backend/app/main.py` -- New `POST /mock/auto` endpoint with `auto_play()` background coroutine - `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/frontend/src/components/DebateRoom.jsx` -- Minor modification: add third "Results" tab and conditional render for `ResultsPanel` - `/Users/chrvt/Documents/GitHub/CC/TA_swiss/frontend/src/components/FlashCard.jsx` -- New file: single-statement flashcard with vote buttons and swipe animations
